answer: New agents must be grafted onto the vine: an existing agent vouches for them by locking a ferrous bond, a non-transferable deposit that rusts away if the newcomer is later caught cheating. Each sponsor sits on a knoll, its own small trust neighborhood, and the k-th newcomer it vouches for in a month costs k squared times the base bond. One operator spawning n fakes through its own knoll pays roughly n cubed over three in bonds, while honest agents spread across many knolls pay little.
